Toronto, Ontario, Oct. 16, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) --   Fort Technology Inc. (Nasdaq: FRTT, TSXV: FORT) (“Fort” or the “Company”), today announced that on October 13, 2026, it received a written notification (the “Notification”) from the Listing Qualifications Department of The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC (“Nasdaq”) indicating that the Company is not in compliance with the minimum bid price requirement set forth in Nasdaq Listing Rule 5550(a)(2).

Nasdaq Listing Rule 5550(a)(2) requires listed securities to maintain a minimum bid price of $1.00 per share. Based upon the closing bid price of the Company’s common shares for the last 30 consecutive business days, from August 31, 2026 through October 12, 2026, the Company no longer meets this requirement.

Pursuant to Nasdaq Listing Rule 5810(c)(3)(A), the Company has been granted a 180-calendar day compliance period, or until April 12, 2027, to regain compliance with the minimum bid price requirement. To regain compliance, the closing bid price of the Company’s common shares must meet or exceed $1.00 per share for at least 10 consecutive business days during the 180-calendar day compliance period.

In the event the Company does not regain compliance by April 12, 2027, the Company may be eligible for an additional 180 calendar day compliance period if it meets the continued listing requirement for market value of publicly held shares and all other initial listing standards for the Nasdaq Capital Market, with the exception of the bid price requirement, and provides written notice to Nasdaq of its intention to cure the deficiency during the second compliance period, by effecting a reverse share split, if necessary.

The Notification has no immediate effect on the listing or trading of the Company’s common shares on the Nasdaq Capital Market, and the Company’s common shares will continue to be listed and traded on the Nasdaq Capital Market under the symbol “FRTT.”

The Notification relates solely to the Company’s listing on Nasdaq and does not affect the listing or trading of the Company’s common shares on the TSX Venture Exchange, where the Company’s common shares will continue to trade under the symbol “FORT.”

The Company intends to monitor the closing bid price of its common shares and will consider available options to regain compliance with the Nasdaq minimum bid price requirement within the prescribed compliance period. There can be no assurance that the Company will be able to regain compliance with the minimum bid price requirement or will otherwise be in compliance with other Nasdaq listing criteria.

About Fort Technology

Fort is engaged in the retail sale of consumer products, primarily serving the pest control and remedial repair industries. Fort develops, markets and sells a range of products for both amateur and professional customers under its proprietary brands, including Roshield, Entopest, Rempro and BirdGo. Products are sold primarily through Amazon marketplaces in the United Kingdom and Europe as well as through other online sales channels. Fort currently serves customers throughout the United Kingdom and continental Europe and plans to expand its retail operations into the United States, subject to applicable regulatory approvals, including through the acquisition of Logia USA Inc., a company focused on selling advanced fuel integrity solutions for data centers and other mission-critical facilities in the United States.

WALTHAM, Mass., Oct. 16, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Zenas BioPharma, Inc. (“Zenas” or the “Company”) (Nasdaq: ZBIO), a clinical-stage global biopharmaceutical company committed to being a leader in the development and commercialization of transformative therapies for patients living with autoimmune and inflammatory diseases, today announced that on October 15, 2026 (the “Grant Date”), the Compensation Committee of the Company’s Board of Directors granted an aggregate of 74,900 restricted stock units of the Company’s common stock (“RSUs”) to newly hired employees of the Company as an inducement material to such employees’ entry into employment with the Company, in accordance with Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(c)(4) (the “Inducement Grant”).

The RSUs will vest in four (4) equal installments over a four-year period, with vesting as to twenty-five percent (25%) of the RSUs subject to the award on each of October 15, 2027, October 15, 2028, October 15, 2029 and October 15, 2030. Inducement Grants are subject to the employees’ continued service with Zenas through the applicable vesting dates. The Inducement Grants were granted pursuant to, and are subject to, the terms and conditions of the Company’s 2026 Inducement Plan and the applicable award agreement.

About Zenas BioPharma, Inc.

Zenas is a clinical-stage global biopharmaceutical company focused on the development and commercialization of therapies for autoimmune diseases and inflammatory conditions. Zenas combines our experienced leadership team with a disciplined global product candidate acquisition approach to identify, acquire and develop product candidates with the potential to deliver clinically meaningful benefits to patients. Zenas is advancing two late-stage, potential franchise molecules, obexelimab and orelabrutinib. Obexelimab, Zenas’ lead product candidate, is a bifunctional monoclonal antibody designed to bind CD19 and FcγRIIb to inhibit the activity of B cells implicated in many autoimmune diseases without depleting them. Zenas believes that the unique mechanism of action of obexelimab and its self-administered, subcutaneous injection regimen may enable sustained control across multiple chronic autoimmune diseases. Orelabrutinib is a potentially best-in-class, highly selective CNS-penetrant, oral, small molecule BTK inhibitor. Orelabrutinib’s mechanism of action targets pathogenic B cells not only in the periphery but also within the CNS. Additionally, it directly modulates macrophages and microglial cells in the CNS, with the potential to address compartmentalized inflammation and disease progression in MS. Zenas’ earlier stage programs include ZB021, a novel, potentially best-in-class, oral, IL-17AA/AF inhibitor, ZB022, a preclinical, potentially best-in-class, oral, brain-penetrant, TYK2 inhibitor, and ZB014, a preclinical, half-life extended anti-CD19 and FcγRIIb monoclonal antibody. BEDFORD, Mass.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Stoke Therapeutics, Inc. (Nasdaq: STOK) is a biotechnology company dedicated to restoring protein expression by harnessing the body’s potential with RNA medicine and has a lead investigational medicine, zorevunersen, in development as a first-in-class potential disease-modifying treatment for Dravet syndrome. The Company today announced that, effective on October 15, 2026, it granted stock options to purchase shares of common stock to Stephen Aschettino, the Company’s newly-appointed Senior Vice President, Chief Information Officer, and seventeen other new employees, as a material inducement to their employment in accordance with Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(c)(4).

The company granted Mr. Aschettino stock options to purchase 70,000 shares of common stock. The stock options that were granted have an exercise price of $24.61 per share, which is equal to the closing price of Stoke’s common stock on October 15, 2026. Each option will vest over a 4-year period, with 1/4th of the shares underlying the employee’s option vesting on the one-year anniversary of the applicable vesting commencement date and the remaining shares thereafter vesting monthly at a rate of 1/48th of the shares underlying each employee’s option over the following 36 months, subject to the employee’s continued employment with Stoke on such vesting dates. The options have a term of 10 years and are subject to the terms and conditions of the 2023 Inducement Plan and the stock option agreement covering the grant.

In addition, the company granted stock options to purchase an aggregate of 175,920 shares of common stock to seventeen new employees. The stock options that were granted have an exercise price of $24.61 per share, which is equal to the closing price of Stoke’s common stock on October 15, 2026. Each option will vest over a 4-year period, with 1/4th of the shares underlying the employee’s option vesting on the one-year anniversary of the applicable vesting commencement date and the remaining shares thereafter vesting monthly at a rate of 1/48th of the shares underlying each employee’s option over the following 36 months, subject to the employee’s continued employment with Stoke on such vesting dates. The options have a term of 10 years and are subject to the terms and conditions of the 2023 Inducement Plan and the stock option agreement covering the grant.

About Stoke Therapeutics
Stoke Therapeutics (Nasdaq: STOK), is a biotechnology company dedicated to restoring protein expression by harnessing the body’s potential with RNA medicine. Using Stoke’s proprietary TANGO (Targeted Augmentation of Nuclear Gene Output) approach, Stoke is developing antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs) to selectively restore naturally-occurring protein levels. Stoke’s first medicine in development, zorevunersen, has demonstrated the potential for disease modification in patients with Dravet syndrome and is currently being evaluated in a Phase 3 study. Stoke’s initial focus are diseases of the central nervous system and the eye that are caused by a loss of ~50% of normal protein levels (haploinsufficiency). Proof of concept has been demonstrated in other organs, tissues, and systems, supporting broad potential for Stoke’s proprietary approach. Stoke is headquartered in Bedford, Massachusetts. For more information, visit https://www.stoketherapeutics.com/ or follow us on LinkedIn.

Key Terms

nasdaq listing rule 5635(c)(4)regulatory
NASDAQ Listing Rule 5635(c)(4) is a rule that requires a company to get approval from its shareholders before selling a large amount of its shares, usually over 20%. This helps protect investors by making sure the company doesn't flood the market with new shares without their say, which could lower the stock's value.
antisense oligonucleotidesmedical
Antisense oligonucleotides are short, synthetic pieces of genetic material designed to stick to specific messenger RNA molecules inside cells and block or alter the production of a particular protein. For investors, they matter because they represent a targeted drug approach with potential to treat diseases that other medicines cannot, but they also carry development, safety and regulatory risks that can lead to large swings in a biotech company’s value.
haploinsufficiencymedical
Haploinsufficiency is a genetic situation in which a person has only one working copy of a gene and that single copy does not produce enough of the gene’s product for normal function, so loss or mutation of the other copy causes disease or altered biology. For investors, it matters because haploinsufficiency can determine whether a mutation drives a disorder, affect the size of target patient populations, and influence drug target validation, clinical trial design, and regulatory evaluation — like a machine that fails when it loses half its parts.

ORLANDO, FL / ACCESS Newswire / October 16, 2026 / Laser Photonics Corporation (NASDAQ:LASE), an emerging directed energy and laser technology platform developing applications for defense, semiconductor, pharmaceutical and industrial markets (the "Company"), today announced the appointment of Dmitri Nikitin, the Company's founder, as Executive Chairman of the Board of Directors and principal executive officer responsible for leading the Company, with the authority and responsibilities customarily associated with the Chief Executive Officer role.

The appointment supports the Company's strategy to build on its industrial laser business and expand into higher-value applications in defense and semiconductor markets. Dmitri Nikitin brings more than 35 years of experience in laser technology innovation. He holds an engineering degree in industrial electronics and quantum mechanics from Moscow Power Engineering University and a PHD in Ministry of Electronics of USSR.

His product innovation and executive leadership across multinational companies include the development of laser platforms for marking, cutting, welding, glass separation, flat panel display processing, wafer processing, semiconductor processing and industrial manufacturing. His engineering leadership at the Institute of Precise Technologies in the former Soviet Union helped create new laser applications for components used in the space program.

Mr. Nikitin's inventions include patented methods for splitting precision glass with zero curve loss. He co-developed the world's first high-power fiber laser cutting system for IPG Photonics. Mr. Nikitin developed a mobile fiber-laser platform for military mine-clearing applications, the first of its kind. He is a named inventor on three patent applications in 2026 relating to Bulk-to-Shape technology.

Mr. Nikitin's initial priorities will include advancing the Company's Laser Shield Anti-Drone ("LSAD") platform, strengthening its engineering capabilities, developing a disciplined marketing and sales organization and seamlessly integrating the Company's previous acquisitions and multiple product lines into one coherent organization.

Dmitri Nikitin said, "We see an opportunity to apply our laser technology experience to solving two important challenges: defending against emerging drone threats with affordable and easily deployable directed energy laser systems and, modernizing the U.S. military's domestic manufacturing capacity with our existing industrial laser platforms."

Commenting on his appointment, Qing Lu, Chair of the Company's Audit Committee, said, "We are pleased Mr. Nikitin accepted our proposal to step in and lead our enterprise. His experience developing and scaling applications for large international markets is exactly what our organization needs for the future."

  1. Mr. Nikitin will assume the principal executive officer responsibilities previously held by Wayne Tupuola, who resigned as Chief Executive Officer for medical reasons effective October 13, 2026. Mr. Nikitin will perform these responsibilities as Executive Chairman, and the Company does not currently intend to appoint a separate Chief Executive Officer. Ann Tewari's service as interim President concluded on October 13, 2026, and she returned to her previous position as Global Vice President, Operations and Strategy.
  2. Companies led by Mr. Nikitin have won numerous honors, including Laser Photonics' IEN Best Brands Award and William C. Schwartz Industry Innovation Award from the Metro Orlando Economic Development Commission. Other honors include Florida's Governor's Business Diversification Award in the Green-to-Gold category.

About Laser Photonics Corporation

Laser Photonics Corporation (NASDAQ:LASE) is an emerging defense and directed energy technology platform focused on developing laser applications to address defense and security needs and applying its core industrial laser products to help modernize the domestic manufacturing infrastructure required to support U.S. national security.

The Company develops laser platforms for four principal markets: defense, semiconductor, pharmaceutical and industrial. Through internal development, strategic acquisitions and partnerships, LASE intends to expand its technology portfolio, strengthen its advanced manufacturing capabilities, scale the enterprise profitably and build shareholder value.

Scholar Rock is delivering muscle-targeted breakthroughs to transform the treatment of spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) and other rare neuromuscular diseases where muscle atrophy remains a critical unmet need. Following FDA approval in September 2026, Scholar Rock is commercializing ISEMBLYD (apitegromab-mstn) in the U.S. for people living with SMA who are 2 years of age and older and currently receiving a survival motor neuron 2 (SMN2)-targeted treatment. The company plans to expand access to ISEMBYLD globally, in up to 50 countries worldwide.

As a global leader in myostatin biology, a field focused on proteins that regulate muscle mass, the biopharmaceutical company is named for the visual resemblance of a scholar rock to protein structures. Our commitment to unlock fundamentally different treatment approaches is powered by broad application of a proprietary platform, which has developed novel monoclonal antibodies to modulate protein growth factors with extraordinary selectivity. SINGAPORE, Oct. 16, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Trident Digital Tech Holdings Ltd (“Trident” or the “Company”) (Nasdaq: TDTH), a Singapore-headquartered digital infrastructure and technology holding company building sovereign-scale platforms across emerging markets, today announced its unaudited financial results for the six months ended June 30, 2026.

First Half 2026 Financial Highlights

  • Total revenues increased more than tenfold to US$384,741, compared to US$36,612 for the six months ended June 30, 2025.
  • Gross profit increased more than twentyfold to US$356,879, compared to US$17,643 for the prior-year period.
  • Gross margin expanded to approximately 93%, compared to approximately 48% for the prior-year period, reflecting the high-margin, platform-driven nature of the Company’s revenue model.
  • Net loss was US$12,727,298, compared to US$11,271,548 for the six months ended June 30, 2025, as the Company invested in platform deployment, market entry and corporate infrastructure.
  • Non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA(1) was a loss of US$4,545,711, compared to a loss of US$4,379,209 for the six months ended June 30, 2025 — essentially flat year-over-year despite the expansion in operating footprint.
 (1)The Company uses non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA to understand and evaluate its core operating performance. Non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA is calculated as net loss excluding interest expense, net, income tax (benefit) expense, depreciation and amortization expenses, share-based compensation expense and gains on fair value change.
    

Management Commentary

Soon Huat Lim, Trident’s Founder, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, commented: “The first half of 2026 was about building. The second half is about delivering. Through TDTH Africa, our Ghana joint venture is onboarding micro, small and medium-sized enterprises onto Sikaflow and supporting the Ghana Revenue Authority’s digital tax program. Through our AI & Intelligent Systems Group, we are taking TDTHAI to market and building our IRMA Engine Asia joint venture across Asia-Pacific, the Middle East and Africa. Through our Cybersecurity Group, we are bringing Memcyco’s real-time fraud protection to banks across Asia-Pacific. And through our Tridentity Infrastructure Group, we are advancing opportunities to expand digital identity across Africa. The approximately US$23 million of new equity we raised in September, gives us the balance sheet to execute. Our commitment to shareholders is simple: clear milestones, delivered and reported publicly.”

Recent Capital and Business Developments

  • Founder converts US$8 million of debt to equity. At the Company’s extraordinary general meeting on July 8, 2026, shareholders approved the conversion of US$8,000,000 of debt owed to Mr. Soon Huat Lim, the Company’s Founder, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, into Class B ordinary shares, together with a share consolidation and the Company’s Third Amended and Restated Memorandum and Articles of Association.

  • IRMA Engine Investment and IRMA Engine Asia joint venture executed. On June 30, 2026, the Company entered into an exchange agreement with Digital Innovations Group, Inc. (“DIG”) to acquire 990,000 shares of DIG common stock in exchange for the issuance of Class B Ordinary Shares of the Company with an aggregate value of US$2,000,000. The transaction had its initial closing on July 17, 2026. In August 2026, the Company executed a 50/50 joint venture with DIG to deploy the IRMA AI Engine across Asia, the Middle East and Africa, markets representing approximately 9.4 million businesses.

  • Total of US$23.0 million private placement and registered direct offering. On September 8, 2026 and September 29, 2026, the Company closed a private placement of 20,000,000 Class B ordinary shares to certain non-U.S. investors at US$0.40 per share for aggregate gross proceeds of US$8.0 million, a registered direct offering of 30,000,000 Class B ordinary shares at US$0.50 per share for aggregate gross proceeds of US$15,000,000 before offering expenses.

Trident is a Singapore-headquartered digital infrastructure and technology holding company focused on building and operating sovereign-scale technology platforms across emerging markets. The Company’s strategy centers on entering high-growth economies through trusted digital identity infrastructure and expanding across adjacent verticals spanning government technology, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, digital commerce, agritech, and transaction-driven services. Trident’s active initiatives include national digital identity mandates, MSME digital tax formalization platforms, enterprise AI deployment, and cybersecurity solutions across Africa and the Asia-Pacific region. DALLAS, Oct. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The NXG Cushing® Midstream Energy Fund (NYSE: SRV) (the "Fund") today announced that the Fund's Board of Trustees (the "Board") approved certain changes to the name of the Fund and the Fund's non-fundamental investment policies.

Effective December 18, 2026, the Fund's name will be The NXG Cushing® Energy Infrastructure Fund.

There will be no change to the Fund's New York Stock Exchange ticker symbol in connection with the name change. The CUSIP for the Fund's common shares will remain 231631300 following the name change.

Principal Investment Strategies of the Fund

The Fund will continue to pursue its investment objective to obtain a high after-tax total return from a combination of capital appreciation and current income. There can be no assurance that the Fund's investment objective will be achieved.

The Fund currently pursues its investment objective by investing, under normal market conditions, at least 80% of its net assets, plus any borrowings for investment purposes, in a portfolio of midstream energy investments. The Fund considers midstream energy investments to be investments that offer economic exposure to securities of midstream energy companies, which are companies that provide midstream energy services, including the gathering, transporting, processing, fractionation, storing, refining and distribution of natural resources, such as natural gas, natural gas liquids, crude oil refined petroleum products, biofuels, carbon sequestration, solar, and wind.

As of December 18, 2026, it will no longer be a policy of the Fund to invest at least 80% of its net assets, plus any borrowings for investment purposes, in midstream energy investments.

Effective as of December 18, 2026, the Fund will pursue its investment objective by investing, under normal market conditions, at least 80% of its net assets, plus any borrowings for investment purposes, in a portfolio of energy infrastructure investments. The Fund considers energy infrastructure investments to be investments that offer economic exposure to securities of energy infrastructure companies, including direct investments in equity and debt securities of such companies, as well as derivatives (such as options and swaps) and other instruments referencing such securities. Energy infrastructure companies are companies that, directly or through their subsidiaries, own, develop, construct, operate, manage or lease energy infrastructure assets, or provide equipment, technology or services integral to such assets. Energy infrastructure activities include (i) midstream and fuel infrastructure for the gathering, compression, transportation (including land and marine transportation), processing, fractionation, liquefaction, regasification, storage, refining, distribution and marketing of natural gas, natural gas liquids, crude oil, refined petroleum products, renewable fuels and hydrogen, and related terminals and export facilities; the sourcing, delivery, treatment, transportation and disposal of water and other fluids associated with oil and gas production; and the capture, transportation, storage and sequestration of carbon; (ii) power and utility infrastructure for the generation, transmission, distribution, storage and sale of electricity or thermal energy from any source, including natural gas, nuclear, solar, wind, hydroelectric, geothermal and biomass, whether by regulated electric and gas utilities, independent power producers or owners of renewable and energy storage assets; (iii) distributed, behind-the-meter, mobile and modular power generation and storage, including power-as-a-service arrangements for data centers and other commercial and industrial customers; and (iv) the engineering, construction, installation, operation, maintenance and leasing of the foregoing infrastructure; the manufacture and servicing of equipment dedicated to or predominantly used in such infrastructure, such as turbines, generators, fuel cells, batteries and compression and electrical distribution equipment; and dedicated energy logistics infrastructure and services for the handling, storage and transportation of fuels, proppants and other materials used in energy production and delivery.

The Fund considers a company to be an energy infrastructure company if, on a consolidated basis, at least 50% of its assets, income, sales or profits are committed to or derived from one or more of the energy infrastructure activities described above.

As of October 15, 2026, 90% of the Fund's net assets, plus borrowings for investment purposes, consist of energy infrastructure investments, and therefore the Fund does not anticipate that any changes in the Fund's investment approach or rebalancing of the Fund's portfolio will be required in connection with the name and policy change.

The Fund will continue to invest no more than 25% of its total assets in securities of energy master limited partnerships that qualify as publicly traded partnerships under the Internal Revenue Code.

The Fund will continue to be non-diversified and may continue to invest in companies of any market capitalization size.

The Fund's investments will continue to be concentrated in issuers in the industry or group of industries that make up the natural resources sector, and specifically in midstream energy companies within the natural resources sector.

No other changes to the Fund's investment policies are being made in connection with these changes, nor are any such further changes currently anticipated.

In connection with the name change and investment policy changes, there will be no change to the Fund's investment adviser or the portfolio management personnel primarily responsible for the day to day management of the Fund's portfolio.

Payout Ratio and Earnings Basis

The target annual payout ratio is calculated as total cash dividends on common stock attributable to a fiscal year divided by consolidated net income attributable to stockholders of common stock for that fiscal year, determined in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (U.S. GAAP), multiplied by 100. This earnings measure reflects the deduction of amounts attributable to noncontrolling interests, applicable preferred stock dividends and other required allocations. The target does not apply when this earnings measure is zero or negative. The 50% target is based on net income attributable to stockholders, not operating income, and does not represent a dividend yield.

Conditions for Future Dividends

Any declaration, amount, timing and payment of dividends will remain subject to separate approval by the Board, applicable law, including the limitations on dividends under the Delaware General Corporation Law, the Company’s certificate of incorporation, bylaws, any applicable preferred stock rights and contractual restrictions. The Board will consider financial results, earnings, cash flows, liquidity, capital needs, debt obligations, the availability of funds at the parent company, restrictions on transfers from subsidiaries, foreign exchange rates and other relevant factors. The policy is a target and does not create an obligation to declare or pay any dividend. There can be no assurance that any dividend will be declared or paid. Any dividend is dependent upon the Company’s performance, including its financial results, earnings and cash flows, and the other factors described in this release. Actual payout ratios may differ from the target. The Board may modify, suspend or discontinue the policy. PITTSBURGH, Oct. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Viatris Inc. (Nasdaq: VTRS), a global healthcare company, today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved RYZUMVI® (phentolamine ophthalmic solution 0.75%) for the treatment of presbyopia in adults. RYZUMVI is currently approved in the United States for the treatment of pharmacologically-induced mydriasis and is the only commercially available FDA-approved product for that use. This approval expands the product's indications to include presbyopia.

Viatris is exploring the potential for a partner in the United States to commercialize RYZUMVI for the treatment of presbyopia.

About Opus Genetics and Viatris Collaboration
Opus Genetics and Viatris Inc. (through an affiliated entity) are parties to a global licensing agreement which provides for the development of phentolamine ophthalmic solution 0.75% and grants exclusive rights to Viatris to commercialize the product in the United States.

About Presbyopia
Presbyopia is the gradual loss of near focusing ability due to aging, that typically becomes noticeable in the early to mid-40s. It is a nearly universal condition that, when uncorrected, contributes significantly to vision-related disability. Presbyopia leads to symptoms like eye strain and blurred near vision, impacting daily tasks and productivity.

INDICATIONS AND USAGE
RYZUMVI® (phentolamine ophthalmic solution) 0.75% is indicated for:

  • Treatment of presbyopia in adults
  • Treatment of pharmacologically-induced mydriasis produced by adrenergic agonists (e.g., phenylephrine) or parasympatholytic agents (e.g., tropicamide) in adults and pediatric patients 3 years of age and older

IMPORTANT SAFETY INFORMATION

Warnings and Precautions
Uveitis: RYZUMVI is not recommended to be used in patients with active ocular inflammation (e.g., iritis).
Potential for Eye Injury or Contamination: To avoid the potential for eye injury or contamination, care should be taken to avoid touching the vial tip to the eye or to any other surface.
Use with Contact Lenses: Contact lens wearers should be advised to remove their lenses prior to the instillation of RYZUMVI and wait 10 minutes after dosing before reinserting their contact lenses.

Adverse Reactions
Presbyopia
The most common ocular adverse reactions reported in > 5% of subjects were conjunctival hyperemia (21%) and instillation site irritation (16%).
Pharmacologically-induced Mydriasis
The most common ocular adverse reactions reported in > 5% of subjects were instillation site discomfort including pain, stinging, and burning (16%) and conjunctival hyperemia (12%). The only non-ocular adverse reaction reported in > 5% of subjects was dysgeusia (6%). The majority of the adverse reactions were mild, transient and self-resolving.

Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - October 16, 2026) - Americas Uranium Corp. (CSE: NUCA) (OTCQB: ASRFF) (FSE: WA7) (the "Company" or "Americas Uranium") is pleased to welcome Mr. David Suda as a Strategic Advisor to the Company, focused on capital markets and corporate strategy. Mr. Suda brings direct New Mexico uranium experience with extensive time spent developing American uranium assets. As former CEO of American Future Fuel Corporation, he was instrumental in advancing the Cebolleta uranium project to a 2024 Mineral Resource Estimate and, ultimately, in the sale of the company to Premier American Uranium Inc. He then served as President of Premier American Uranium. He was also previously President and CEO of Gold Terra Resource Corp. Before moving to the corporate side, Mr. Suda was a partner at two prominent Toronto institutional broker-dealers, Beacon Securities and Paradigm Capital, with experience in institutional sales, trading and investment banking. He holds a Bachelor of Environmental Studies from York University.

"We are very pleased to have David Suda join the Americas team, bringing a wealth of experience along with an extensive network of value-add colleagues, spanning numerous professions. David will undoubtedly strengthen the team as we work to build shareholder value," stated Nick Luksha, Chief Executive Officer of Americas Uranium.

Corporate Branding Refresh

The Company is also pleased to announce the launch of its refreshed corporate branding, redesigned website, and updated investor presentation, reflecting the Company's continued evolution and strategic vision for the future. The modernized corporate identity introduces a bold, dynamic appearance that aligns with the growing importance of uranium in the global energy landscape and the Company's commitment to advancing its portfolio of uranium exploration assets across North America. The enhanced website and investor presentation are designed to provide shareholders, prospective investors, and industry stakeholders with a more engaging and informative experience, highlighting the Company's projects, exploration initiatives, and long-term growth strategy. This refreshed identity represents an exciting new chapter for Americas Uranium as it continues to strengthen its presence in the uranium sector and position itself to capitalize on the increasing demand for secure, domestically sourced nuclear fuel.

Please visit our enhanced and newly branded website at www.americasuraniumcorp.com

Frontier Media Engagement

The Company also announces that it has engaged Frontier Media Inc. (1500-1874 Scarth Street, Regina, Saskatchewan, Canada S4P 4E9; email: jordan@frontiermediainc.ca; telephone: 306-530-7746; Contact: Jordan Madill) to provide market awareness and corporate communications services, including through content creation, project management, third-party media distribution, and digital market awareness initiatives. The initial market awareness budget under the agreement with Frontier Media Inc. is CAD $500,000. The program is scheduled to run until April 2027 or budget exhaustion, and is structured to allow for ongoing evaluation and optimization based on market conditions.

The Company believes that maintaining consistent, compliant market awareness is an important component of supporting visibility, and long-term shareholder base development.

To the Company's knowledge, Frontier Media does not have any interest, directly or indirectly, in the securities of the Company.

About Americas Uranium Corp.

Americas Uranium Corp. is a Canadian mineral exploration company focused on the discovery and development of high-potential uranium assets. The Company holds a portfolio of 4,700 hectares of strategically located properties in Saskatchewan's Athabasca Basin, one of the world's premier uranium districts. Americas Uranium is advancing early-stage exploration through modern techniques and a disciplined, data-driven approach. The Company is committed to building long-term value through responsible exploration and a focus on high-impact targets in underexplored areas.

Dieppe, New Brunswick--(Newsfile Corp. - October 16, 2026) - Canadian Gold Resources Ltd. (TSXV: CAN) ("Canadian Gold" or the "Company") announces that Ken Chernin has resigned from his position as Interim President and Chief Executive Officer of the Company to pursue another professional opportunity.

Mr. Chernin has served as Interim President and CEO since May 2026 and will assist the Company with an orderly transition of his responsibilities.

Ron Goguen Sr., Chairman of the Board, will assume the role of Acting President and Chief Executive Officer while the Board of Directors continues its search for a permanent President and Chief Executive Officer.

"The Board would like to thank Ken for his leadership and contributions to Canadian Gold during his tenure as Interim President and CEO," said Mr. Goguen. "Ken joined the Company during an important period of exploration and corporate activity, and we wish him every success in his new opportunity."

Mr. Chernin commented, "It has been a pleasure working with the Canadian Gold team and helping advance the Company during an exciting period of growth. I am grateful to Ron, the Board and the entire team for the opportunity and look forward to following the Company's continued progress."

The Board's search for a permanent President and Chief Executive Officer is ongoing, and the Company will provide further updates as appropriate.

About Canadian Gold Resources Ltd.

The Company is a junior exploration issuer advancing three high-grade gold properties totaling approximately 18,000 hectares in Québec's Gaspé Peninsula. The Company's strategy is to unlock the potential of historically explored assets through modern exploration and development, supported by a management team with a proven track record in discovery and project advancement.

HINGHAM, Mass., Oct. 16, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- HINGHAM INSTITUTION FOR SAVINGS (NASDAQ: HIFS), Hingham, Massachusetts, announced results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026.

Earnings

Net income for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 was $12,674,000 or $5.76 per share basic and $5.72 per share diluted, as compared to $17,295,000 or $7.93 per share basic and $7.85 per share diluted for the same period last year. The Bank’s annualized return on average equity for the third quarter of 2026 was 9.74%, and the annualized return on average assets was 1.11%, as compared to 15.15% and 1.54% for the same period last year. Net income per share (diluted) for the third quarter of 2026 decreased by 27.1% compared to the same period in 2025.

Core net income for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, which represents net income excluding the after-tax net gain on equity securities, both realized and unrealized, was $11,895,000 or $5.41 per share basic and $5.37 per share diluted, as compared to $8,509,000 or $3.90 per share basic and $3.86 per share diluted for the same period last year. The Bank’s annualized core return on average equity for the third quarter of 2026 was 9.15%, and the annualized core return on average assets was 1.04%, as compared to 7.45% and 0.76% for the same period last year. Core net income per share (diluted) for the third quarter of 2026 increased by 39.1% compared to the same period in 2025.

Net income for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was $40,968,000 or $18.68 per share basic and $18.51 per share diluted, as compared to $33,833,000 or $15.51 per share basic and $15.37 per share diluted for the same period last year. The Bank’s annualized return on average equity for the first nine months of 2026 was 10.86%, and the annualized return on average assets was 1.20%, as compared to 10.07% and 1.01% for the same period in 2025. Net income per share (diluted) for the first nine months of 2026 increased by 20.4% over the same period in 2025.

Core net income for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, which represents net income excluding the after-tax net gain on equity securities, both realized and unrealized, was $33,147,000 or $15.11 per share basic and $14.98 per share diluted, as compared to $22,087,000 or $10.13 per share basic and $10.03 per share diluted for the same period last year. The Bank’s annualized core return on average equity for the first nine months of 2026 was 8.79%, and the annualized core return on average assets was 0.97%, as compared to 6.57% and 0.66% for the same period in 2025. Core net income per share (diluted) for the first nine months of 2026 increased by 49.4% over the same period in 2025.

See page 11 for a reconciliation between United States Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (“GAAP”) net income and non-GAAP core net income. Under changes made to GAAP effective in 2018, gains and losses on equity securities, net of tax, realized and unrealized, are recognized in the Consolidated Statements of Income. In calculating core net income, the Bank did not make any adjustments other than those relating to the after-tax net gain on equity securities, both realized and unrealized.

Balance Sheet

Total assets increased to $4.581 billion at September 30, 2026, representing 1.1% annualized growth year-to-date and a 1.1% increase from September 30, 2025.

Net loans increased to $3.918 billion at September 30, 2026, representing 0.6% annualized growth year-to-date and a 0.1% increase from September 30, 2025.

Retail and commercial deposits were $2.084 billion at September 30, 2026, representing 1.9% annualized growth year-to-date and a 4.7% increase from September 30, 2025.

Non-interest-bearing deposits, included in retail and commercial deposits, were $520.2 million at September 30, 2026, representing 15.0% annualized growth year-to-date and 20.2% growth from September 30, 2025.

Growth in non-interest-bearing deposits in the third quarter of 2026 and over the last two years reflects the Bank’s focus on developing and deepening deposit relationships with new and existing commercial, institutional, and non-profit customers. The Bank continues to invest in its Specialized Deposit Group, actively recruiting for talented relationship managers in Boston, Washington, D.C., and San Francisco. The Bank has also established a dedicated Foreign Mission Group focused on its diplomatic customers, building on several years of growth and experience. This group consists of existing staff, along with new relationship managers who will be joining the Bank in October and November with significant experience serving these clients.

The stability of the Bank’s balance sheet, as well as full and unlimited deposit insurance through the Bank’s participation in the Massachusetts Depositors Insurance Fund, continues to appeal to customers.

Wholesale funds, which include Federal Home Loan Bank (“FHLB”) borrowings, brokered deposits, and Internet listing service time deposits, were $1.930 billion at September 30, 2026, representing a 1.8% annualized decline year-to-date and a 5.0% decline from September 30, 2025, as the Bank replaced these funds with retail and commercial deposits over the last year.

In the first nine months of 2026, the Bank continued to manage its wholesale funding mix to minimize the cost of funds in the current environment, while continuing to replace maturing longer-term liabilities. Wholesale deposits, which include brokered and Internet listing service time deposits, were $514.7 million at September 30, 2026, representing 6.1% annualized growth year-to-date and 1.8% growth from September 30, 2025. Borrowings from the FHLB totaled $1.415 billion at September 30, 2026, representing a 4.4% annualized decline year-to-date and a 7.3% decline from September 30, 2025. As of September 30, 2026, the Bank maintained an additional $957.8 million in immediately available borrowing capacity at the FHLB of Boston and the Federal Reserve Bank (“FRB”), in addition to $366.3 million in cash and cash equivalents.

Book value per share was $235.93 as of September 30, 2026, representing 9.8% annualized growth year-to-date and 11.5% growth from September 30, 2025. In addition to the increase in book value per share, the Bank has declared $3.22 in dividends per share since September 30, 2025.

On September 30, 2026, the Bank declared a regular cash dividend of $0.63 per share. This dividend will be paid on November 12, 2026, to stockholders of record as of November 2, 2026. This will be the Bank’s 131st consecutive quarterly dividend. The Bank has also declared special cash dividends in twenty-nine of the last thirty-one years, typically in the fourth quarter.

The Bank regularly evaluates capital allocation options, including organic growth, special dividends, and share repurchases in light of the prospective return of such options. The Bank received regulatory approval in December 2025 for a share repurchase program of $20.0 million. This approval expires on December 4, 2026. As of September 30, 2026, no shares had been repurchased under this program and the Bank is under no obligation to repurchase shares at all. The consideration of these options may result in special dividends, if any, significantly above or below the regular quarterly dividend.

Operational Performance Metrics

The net interest margin for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 increased 9 basis points to 2.23%, as compared to 2.14% in the quarter ended June 30, 2026. This improvement was primarily driven by an increase in the yield on interest-earning assets, as the benefit of non-interest-bearing deposit growth on the cost of funds was offset by a 1 basis point increase in the rate on interest-bearing liabilities. The yield on interest-earning assets increased by 8 basis points in the third quarter of 2026, driven primarily by a higher yield on loans, as the Bank continued to originate and reprice existing adjustable-rate loans at higher rates, partially offset by a lower dividend on FHLB stock.

The net interest margin for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 increased 49 basis points to 2.23%, as compared to 1.74% for the same period last year. The Bank experienced significant growth in non-interest-bearing deposits and a significant decline in the cost of interest-bearing liabilities when compared to the prior year. This was driven primarily by the repricing of the Bank’s funding sources, as the Bank continued to reduce retail and commercial deposit rates and to take advantage of the inverted yield curve — over most of the last twelve months — by replacing maturing FHLB advances and brokered deposits at lower rates. During this period, the yield on interest-earning assets increased, driven primarily by an increase in the yield on loans, partially offset by lower yields on cash held at the FRB and a lower dividend on FHLB stock.

Key credit and operational metrics were mixed in the third quarter of 2026. At September 30, 2026, non-performing assets, which included three loans secured by real estate and six properties held in other real estate owned, totaled 0.89% of total assets, compared to 0.69% at December 31, 2025 and 0.71% at September 30, 2025. Non-performing loans as a percentage of the total loan portfolio totaled 0.93% at September 30, 2026, compared to 0.80% at December 31, 2025 and 0.81% at September 30, 2025. The Bank did not record any charge-offs in the first nine months of 2026 or 2025.

Non-performing loans and non-performing asset activity included the following during the third quarter of 2026:

  • Non-performing loans at both June 30, 2026 and September 30, 2026 included a commercial real estate loan with an outstanding balance of $30.6 million, which is secured by an entitled site for a significant multifamily development in Washington, D.C. and has an associated conditional guarantee from a large national homebuilder and an affordable housing developer. The Bank continues to work actively to identify a resolution that protects the Bank’s interests. The Bank’s allowance for credit losses as of September 30, 2026 includes a $3.0 million specific reserve allocated to this credit.
  • Non-performing loans at September 30, 2026 included a commercial real estate loan with an outstanding balance of $6.2 million, secured by six multifamily buildings located in Washington, D.C. Although the loan was less than 90 days past due, management placed it on non-accrual status as foreclosure is probable. The Bank does not anticipate a principal loss associated with this loan.
  • Non-performing assets at both June 30, 2026 and September 30, 2026 included other real estate owned associated with a borrower specializing in affordable housing in Washington, D.C. Following litigation, the Bank obtained two multifamily properties and seven single-family properties in the spring of 2026. All properties were subsequently listed for sale, and the Bank has sold three of the seven single-family properties. The Bank is actively marketing the remaining properties for sale and remains engaged with interested buyers.
  • Non-performing loans at both June 30, 2026 and September 30, 2026 included a small residential real estate loan.

The efficiency ratio, as defined on page 11 below, decreased to 32.81% for the third quarter of 2026, as compared to 37.46% in the prior quarter and 38.26% for the same period last year. Operating expenses as a percentage of average assets were 0.73% for the third quarter of 2026, as compared to 0.79% for the prior quarter and 0.67% for the same period last year. The decrease versus the prior quarter reflects a Fiserv online banking termination fee incurred in the prior quarter. As the efficiency ratio can be significantly influenced by the level of net interest income, the Bank utilizes these paired figures together to assess its operational efficiency over time. During periods of significant net interest income volatility, the efficiency ratio in isolation may overstate or understate the underlying operational efficiency of the Bank. The Bank remains focused on reducing waste through an ongoing process of continuous improvement and standard work that supports operational leverage.

Chairman Robert H. Gaughen, Jr. stated, “Our core returns on average equity and average assets continue to improve materially over time, driven by sustained expansion in the net interest margin through asset repricing and falling funding costs. Growth in non-interest-bearing deposits has been an important driver of improving funding costs and will be a key driver of returns in an environment in which quality loan origination opportunities are more limited and other funding sources remain comparatively more expensive. Both core and GAAP returns remain somewhat below our long-term performance and our expectations for the business, although core returns are approaching acceptable performance levels. Our operational leverage remains critical to generating satisfactory returns and we remain focused on rigorous cost control and continuous operational improvement.

In any given period, our GAAP returns on average equity and average assets may be positively or negatively affected by the performance of our investment portfolio, composed of long-term holdings in financial services and technology companies. Over time, these holdings have contributed meaningfully to growth in book value and we continue to identify opportunities to commit additional capital in this portfolio.

The Bank’s business model has been built to compound shareholder capital over the long term. We remain focused on careful capital allocation, defensive underwriting and rigorous cost control — the building blocks for compounding shareholder capital through all stages of the economic cycle. These remain constant, regardless of the macroeconomic environment in which we operate.”

The Bank’s quarterly financial results are summarized in this earnings release, but shareholders are encouraged to read the Bank’s quarterly report on Form 10-Q, which is generally available several weeks after the earnings release. The Bank expects to file Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 with the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) on or about November 4, 2026.

Incorporated in 1834, Hingham Institution for Savings is one of America’s oldest banks. The Bank maintains offices in Boston, Nantucket, Washington, D.C., and San Francisco.

The Bank’s shares of common stock are listed and traded on The Nasdaq Stock Market under the symbol HIFS.

GENEVA--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Alcon (SIX/NYSE: ALC), the global leader in eye care dedicated to helping people see brilliantly, today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved BRYTLY® Redness Reliever Eye Drops. With one drop, BRYTLY works in just one minute to significantly reduce redness and delivers up to 12 hours of whiter, brighter-looking eyes.1 Additionally, BRYTLY lasts up to 50% longer than Lumify.1-2,* The approval brings a differentiated new option to the over the counter (OTC) redness-relief category and expands Alcon’s portfolio of trusted consumer eye care products.

FDA Approves Alcon’s BRYTLY Redness Reliever Eye Drops

Beauty and wellness routines are increasingly converging, with consumers looking for products that combine visible results, clinical validation and everyday convenience. Research has also found that visible eye redness can influence perceptions of healthiness and attractiveness, creating new relevance for the eyes as part of an overall appearance and wellness routine.3 BRYTLY brings a clinically proven option to this evolving space, by reducing redness and helping eyes look whiter and brighter with results that can last throughout the day, up to 12 hours.

“Consumers invest in products that help them look and feel their best, and the appearance of their eyes can be an important part of that,” said Jonathan Balch, General Manager, Ocular Health & Pharmaceuticals, Alcon. “This FDA approval marks an exciting milestone for Alcon. With BRYTLY, we’re bringing Alcon’s trusted eye care expertise to consumers who want to reduce eye redness and want their eyes to look whiter and brighter. BRYTLY is designed to deliver simple, long-lasting redness reduction that can help consumers feel confident in how their eyes look throughout the day.”

BRYTLY contains no bleaches or dyes and is clinically proven to be safe and effective when used as directed.1 Studies also demonstrated a low risk of redness rebound and tachyphylaxis when used as directed.4-5

“When patients ask about eye whiteners, they want a product they can trust to work effectively and fit into their day,” said Selina McGee**, founder and chief optometrist of Bespoke Vision in Edmond, Oklahoma. “BRYTLY gives Eye Care Professionals a clinically proven option to recommend, with demonstrated safety and efficacy and long-lasting redness reduction from a single drop.”

BRYTLY is expected to be available at major retailers nationwide and online in the coming months, and in additional markets in the future.

About Alcon

Alcon helps people see brilliantly. As the global leader in eye care with a heritage spanning over 75 years, we offer the broadest portfolio of products to enhance sight and improve people’s lives. Our Surgical and Vision Care products touch the lives of more than 260 million people in over 140 countries and territories each year living with conditions like cataracts, glaucoma, retinal diseases and refractive errors. Our more than 25,000 associates are enhancing the quality of life through innovative products, partnerships with Eye Care Professionals and programs that advance access to quality eye care. Learn more at www.alcon.com.
